summary: Network interface ordering change triggers certificate-based VPN failure after imaging
description:
Issue summary: After standard depot-imaging using the 2026.03 corporate image, a subset of laptops fail to establish our corporate certificate-based VPN (CertVPN) post-provisioning. Impact: Affected devices cannot access internal services; users report "no valid certificate" errors in the VPN client and helpdesk sees enrollment loops. Environment: Corporate imaging pipeline (SCCM/ConfigMgr task sequence), corp PKI (HashiCorp Vault-issued machine certs), Windows 11 22H2-based image, post-imaging Company MDM (Intune) enrollment.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Pick a device (Dell 7440 or Lenovo X1) out of depot stock.
2) Boot PXE and run depot image 2026.03 via SCCM TS.
3) Device completes imaging, reboots to OOBE, auto-enrolls in Intune.
4) Run corporate baseline scripts including network drivers and Cisco AnyConnect (CertVPN) config.
5) Attempt CertVPN connection.

Observed behavior: VPN client reports "Certificate not found / authentication failed". Device local cert store shows machine cert present, but VPN logs indicate certificate selection failed and the system network interface used for the initial machine cert request is not the expected physical NIC but a virtual NIC created by the docking/Thunderbolt controller. Expected behavior: Machine certificate selection succeeds and VPN establishes automatically after network is available.

Additional notes: Issue is intermittent (~6-8% of imaged units) and correlates with devices docked during depot imaging or with dual NICs present. Not seen when devices are imaged unattached to docks. No prior reports before the 2026.03 image rollout.
logs:
Attached excerpts:
- VPN client log (AnyConnect): "Cert selection failed: no matching cert on interface {vEthernet0}" timestamp 2026-03-13T10:22:14Z
- System event log: Schannel warnings during TLS handshake to authproxy: 0x8009030e
- Imaging task sequence log: network drivers applied: 2026-03-13T09:58:02Z (netwtw10 v22.60)
- Intune enrollment debug: TPM attestation succeeded; machine cert requested from PKI endpoint, cert issued but final step reported 'scope mismatch' in orchestration logs.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by SRE: reproduced on a lab Dell docked to TB4 dock and on Lenovo with an external USB-C NIC. Observed interface list order differs: virtual adapter enumerated before physical Ethernet, which causes machine cert client to bind to wrong interface context during the certificate selection callback. Verified TLS handshake from wrong source IP. Checked SCCM TS: network driver installation order changed in 2026.03 image (new net driver package installs 'virtual switch' driver earlier). Intune MDM profile didn't include interface-scoped certificate selector. Ticket escalated to imaging and network driver owners.
hypothesis: Driver installation order in 2026.03 causes a virtual NIC (or dock vNIC) to enumerate before the physical adapter, which leads to cert enrollment and VPN client picking the wrong interface context, failing client-side policy that expects the cert on physical NIC IP. This only manifests when dock/hub creates virtual NICs or when multiple NICs present during the initial cert bind.
steps_taken: - Re-imaged a affected unit without dock attached: CertVPN worked. - Re-imaged with dock attached reproduces failure. - Swapped driver package order in a local task sequence (deferred virtual switch install to after Intune enrollment) — reproducer passes. - Collected kernel-mode net adapter enumeration timestamps. - Opened a support call with third-party VPN vendor (Cisco AnyConnect) to review cert selection logic.
root_cause: Device/driver enumeration order change in the 2026.03 image caused virtual/dock-created adapters to appear before primary NIC during early boot/enrollment, leading to incorrect interface binding in our cert selection logic and the VPN client.
workaround: Temporary process for depot: ensure devices are imaged off-dock. For already provisioned devices, instruct users to disconnect docks/hubs, reboot, and re-run the 'Corporate Network Repair' script (Intune remediation package) which reinstalls network drivers in the fallback order and forces rebind of machine cert. Documented in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IT/Imaging+Workarounds
resolution: Imaging team to reorder net driver packages in the next 2026.03.1 build (virtual switch drivers deferred). Rolling patch scheduled for 2026-03-16 to update SCCM task sequence. VPN vendor provided a client-side config knob to prefer interface by name; applied as emergency policy for impacted fleet via Intune until patched. Follow-up: update Intune device configuration to avoid interface-scoped cert assumptions.

Miguel Santos (Assignee) 2026-03-13: Confirmed logs attached. Reproduced locally with docked Dell. Marking as P1 and escalating to Imaging + Network driver owners.
Imaging Engineer - Priya Rao 2026-03-13: Investigating change set - discovered net package reorder in 2026.03. Adding to 2026.03.1 fix.
Network Eng - Tomas Eriksson 2026-03-13: Verified interface enumeration timestamps; agrees with root cause. Will coordinate driver reorder test.
SRE - Chen Li 2026-03-14: Deployed Intune emergency remediation to pinned subset; verified VPN connects for previously failing unit after remediation.
next_steps: - Imaging team to build 2026.03.1 with driver order fix and run validation matrix including docked scenarios (owner: Priya Rao) - Network team to add adapter-preference override in corp VPN policy as a config transient (owner: Tomas) - Update Intune device config to avoid interface-scoped cert selection (owner: Security/Endpoint) - Communicate depot imaging stop-gap: no docking during imaging until 2026-03-16 patch.
follow_up_items: Run fleet query to enumerate devices imaged with 2026.03 and report failures (owner: SRE)
Add docking scenarios to CI imaging matrix
Audit other task sequence package ordering for similar enumeration risks
